contexts.text: They who are not in charity are called hardened in forehead, and hard in heart ().
I will harden his heart () = obstinacy... This is said from the appearance... AC 7300. AC 7305. AC 7338. AC 7533.

In the internal sense, it = that not Jehovah, but they themselves hardened their own heart; that is, made themselves obstinate; for it is the evil with a man which hardens or makes him obstinate against Divine things; and evil comes from man...
The heart of Pharaoh was hardened = that from evil they made themselves obstinate... To make the heart heavy, is said from falsity; but to harden the heart, is from evil.
Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh = that the infesters made themselves obstinate. AC 7733. AC 7797.
The spirit, and the heart, = both lives, which are said to be hardened () when there is no will to understand truth and good, or to do them.

Hardened in heart () = those who do not admit good; and therefore those who are in evil... for the heart = the good of love; and a hardened heart = the same as a stony heart; namely, where the good of love is not admitted.
The hardening of faces answereth against them () = the refusal and non-admission of Divine truth and Divine good into the thoughts and affections, which are their interiors.
The faces hardened against their faces () = the rejection of falsity by means of truths; and the forehead hardened against their forehead = the rejection of evil by means of good. (See Hard.)
Thou shalt not see a hardened people () = those who are in falsities from evil; and, abstractedly, those falsities. AE 455:13.
A horrible hardening () = the confirmation of the heart against the truths and goods of the Word.
